To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Q‐Dock, our low‐resolution flexible docking program, can recover on average 15–20% more specific protein–ligand interactions than all‐atom docking methods when the receptor model has an RMSD from the native of 3–4 Å.
Q‐Dock is a fast and robust low‐resolution ligand‐protein docking approach that can utilize low quality receptor models.
Q‐Dock is a low‐resolution protein structure‐based ligand docking method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, implementation and optimization of the Q‐Dock method, which can be used for low‐resolution ligand‐protein docking.
the development of a novel low‐resolution flexible docking algorithm, Q‐Dock, which utilizes pocket‐specific protein models as targets for docking.
developing a new low‐resolution flexible docking approach for ligand docking to low‐quality protein structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
QDock is a very promising approach for ligand docking against low resolution models of protein structures, especially if a pocket specific potential is applied.
, in our opinion, the Q‐Dock approach is the best method for docking ligands into a protein target, if the structure is known with low precision, and the ligand has a known conformation.
, while the Q‐Dock method is very useful for low‐resolution docking, the pocket‐specific interaction potential is very useful to improve the docking accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Q‐Dock method is able to dock a ligand into a protein binding site with low‐quality protein model with high accuracy.
the Q‐Dock method can be used to dock ligands into protein models that have been derived from homology modeling or ab initio modeling.
we have developed a new knowledge‐based potential that improves low‐resolution docking by 6.3 fold.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Q‐Dock can be used to generate a large number of low‐resolution models for a given receptor, and then select the best model for docking using the pocket‐specific potential.
low‐resolution flexible docking is an important and useful tool for docking ligands into predicted protein structures.
low‐resolution flexible docking can be used to predict protein–ligand complexes with high accuracy, even when the protein structure is not known with high accuracy.
